evidence.aggregation_rule: Total lookups summed over the 44 fixed probes for C++ = 32. Mean lookups per site = 32/217 = 0.1475 (site inventory frozen in semantic_site_matrix.json, identical denominator for every language). Score = 100/(1+mean_lookups_per_site) = 100/1.1475 = 87.14, rounded to 87.1.
evidence.basis: all-fragments (single-language shard; common-basis reconciliation performed by aggregator)
evidence.gate_notes: score_requires_comparability_gate (primary.json semantic_compression.fixed_probe_count=44) is satisfied for this shard: all 44 frozen probes evaluated for C++ with a documented lookup count and citation; cross-language common-basis reconciliation (which probes have fragments in ALL ten languages) is performed by the aggregating runner, not by this single-language worker.
evidence.methodology_rule: 6.1.3.C semantic_compression.md: record the number of required external semantic lookups or declaration-graph hops (callee signature, variable/type declaration, overload set, trait/interface/protocol implementation, imported definition, global configuration/compiler mode) needed to resolve each frozen site's semantic fact from C++'s local surface form, under the R10-selected fragment for each probe. Lookups that are optional for extra detail are excluded. Lower total is better.
evidence.normalization_formula: score = 100 / (1 + mean_lookups_per_site), where mean_lookups_per_site = total_external_lookups_across_all_sites / total_sites_in_universe (217 sites across 44 frozen probes). Raw values recorded per probe below; per-site counting follows the same fixed site inventory used for Semantic Density so denominators cannot vary by language.

per_probe_raw_lookup_counts.note: const int n = 7; return n; — fully local, no external declarations consulted.
static (or namespace-scope) int64_t counter = 0; and constexpr int64_t LIMIT = 100; — mutability, lifetime (static storage duration) and representation are all evident from the local declarations.
int32_t v; if(cond){v=5;}else{v=9;} return v; — C++ performs no definite-assignment check; all facts are local.
uint8_t* buf = new uint8_t[16]; — possible_failure (std::bad_alloc) is documented in the standard library, not visible at the call site: 1 lookup (imported definition).
x += 1; — overflow behavior is a fixed language rule (signed overflow UB), not a lookup.
xs[1] = 42; — operator[] semantics are a fixed language/library rule known without consulting a declaration.
int slot=4; int& port=slot; port=9; return slot; — reference aliasing fully local.
std::span<const int> window(xs); — that span never copies and rejects writes is documented library behavior: 1 lookup.
Using std::shared_ptr round-trip through a container and comparing .get() pointers — identity semantics documented in library: 1 lookup.

Bare call f(x): aliasing, mutability, allocation/copy, and externally_visible_side_effects for x cannot be resolved from the call-site syntax alone and require consulting f's declared signature (excluded from the fragment by design, per spec 6.1.4.B): 4 sites x 1 hop each = 4.
put's full declaration (void put(int& cell){cell=12;}) is included inside the measured fragment for this probe, so the writable-alias facts are local.
std::transform(xs.begin(),xs.end(),ys.begin(),neg); — std::transform's application contract (applies neg to each element, does not mutate xs) is documented library behavior: 1 lookup.
mid's full declaration is inside the measured fragment; value/copy semantics of the returned int are local.
std::tuple/structured bindings for divmod2 — that tie/structured-binding decomposition does not copy or share is documented library/language behavior: 1 lookup.
r = a*b+c; — fixed precedence/operator rules, fully local.
q=a/b; m=a%b; d=(double)a/b; — truncation/sign rules are fixed language rules, local.
Checked-mode overflow behavior is pinned by the frozen recipe (no checked-arith facility in C++, so plain operator UB is recorded); no external lookup needed to state that.
Explicit local guard on b==0 — fully local.
s1==s2 for std::string — that operator== compares contents (not identity) is documented library behavior: 1 lookup.
std::sort(xs.rbegin(),xs.rend()) or std::sort with std::greater<>{} — in-place vs new-sequence and comparator contract documented in library: 1 lookup.
static_cast<int32_t>(big) — explicit, fixed conversion rule, local.
sum = i + d; — usual arithmetic conversions are a fixed language rule, local.
xs[i] — operator[] UB-on-out-of-range is a fixed, well known language/library rule, local.
std::span<int> part(xs.data()+1,3) or vector sub-range construction — that it shares storage (does not copy) is documented library behavior: 1 lookup.
std::optional<int> o = std::nullopt; n = o.value_or(0); — value_or's fallback contract is documented library behavior: 1 lookup.
std::optional's transform/and_then short-circuit-on-absence contract is documented library behavior: 1 lookup.

int parse_twice(std::string s){ return 2*std::stoi(s); } — that std::stoi throws std::invalid_argument/out_of_range, and that an uncaught exception propagates to the caller, are documented library/language facts external to the visible call: 2 lookups (possible_failure + control_flow_effect).

try { n = std::stoi(s); } catch(...) { n = 0; } — knowing exactly which exception types std::stoi can throw, and that only the stoi call (not surrounding code) is protected, both require consulting library documentation: 2 lookups.
std::variant<Circle,Rect> declared locally in the fragment; closedness is evident from the local declaration.
std::visit or std::get_if switch over the variant declared in F14.P1's local declaration; exhaustiveness-checking behavior (compile error on unhandled visitor arm) is a fixed language rule.

Multi-unit extension (Tri implementing area() from a separate translation unit) requires consulting the shapes unit's abstract interface declaration and the separate unit's Tri implementation, both external to the calling fragment: 2 lookups.
template<class T> T head(...) — declared locally in the fragment; the T-to-result relationship is evident from the local declaration.
template<class T> requires std::totally_ordered<T> T max_of(T,T) — the constraint is written at the local declaration.
Abstract Named interface and A/B implementations all declared locally within the fragment/unit.
std::accumulate(xs.begin(),xs.end(),0) — accumulate's contract (does not mutate xs, returns fold of elements) is documented library behavior: 1 lookup.
std::unordered_map iteration-order-is-unspecified and .find()-miss handling are documented library facts external to the local code: 1 lookup.

std::ifstream RAII — that the file handle is released deterministically at scope exit (destructor) and that open/read can fail are both documented library facts, not visible in the local fragment: 2 lookups.
struct Handle{ ~Handle(){ ++released; } }; — the destructor hook is declared inside the measured fragment, so its deterministic, exactly-once firing is local.
#include <iostream>; std::cout<<"x\n"; — which names the include introduces and from where is documented in the standard library, external to the fragment: 1 lookup.

util.cpp/util.h with pub_add exported and secret() private (anonymous namespace or static) — the external call site must consult util.h's declaration of pub_add, and the private-boundary enforcement rule is confirmed by consulting util.cpp's internal-linkage declaration: 2 lookups.

std::async/std::future launch+join — the concurrency guarantee (async policy, join semantics, exception propagation through future::get) is documented library behavior external to the visible call syntax: 2 lookups.
std::mutex/std::atomic<int64_t> race-freedom guarantee for the read-modify-write and thread join semantics are both documented library facts external to the local increment statements: 2 lookups.
extern "C" int abs(int); call — the C ABI/calling-convention assumption and abs's documented contract (from <cstdlib>) are external to the bare extern declaration written in the fragment: 1 lookup.

extern "C" int add2(int a,int b){return a+b;} — the export mechanism (extern "C") and its effect on the symbol name are fully evident from the local declaration/annotation; nm verification is mechanical, not an added semantic lookup.
